problem.text: Which graphs obtained by replacing the edges of a graph with even paths or even generalized theta graphs satisfy Sidorenko's conjecture.

claims.text: Theorem 1.3: replacing every edge of a KNRS graph by an even generalized theta graph gives a Sidorenko graph. Theorem 1.4: for an arbitrary base graph H on h vertices, an even-path replacement is Sidorenko under a divisibility condition on the number of paths of each even length (sum over edges divisible by binom(h,2) for every length, or one length only with sum at least binom(h,2)). Corollary 1.5, Theorems 1.6 and 1.7 (clique subdivisions with two path lengths, products of a Sidorenko graph and a KNRS graph), Theorem 1.8 (flowers are KNRS), Proposition 4.2 (uniform subdivisions of Sidorenko graphs are Sidorenko) and Proposition 4.3 (odd generalized theta graphs, sketched). Conjecture 4.1 states that every bipartite subdivision of a Sidorenko graph is Sidorenko.

assumptions.text: The host may be taken to be a d-regular graphon (Lemma 2.2, from Coregliano and Razborov, Theorem 8.2). The KNRS input is the graphon form for d-locally dense graphons (Lemma 2.4, from Bradač, Sudakov and Wigderson) together with Reiher's weighted lemma.

methods.text: Auxiliary graphons that count even paths between two vertices are shown to be locally dense when the host is regular (Lemmas 3.2 and 3.3); a Hölder argument inspired by Conlon and Lee handles the divisibility case (Theorem 1.4); Proposition 4.2 uses t(H',W) = t(H, W^(l+1)).

evidence.text: Complete proofs for Theorems 1.3, 1.4, 1.7 and 1.8 and Proposition 4.2; Proposition 4.3 has a proof sketch.

limitations.text: Every subdivision and theta result before this paper needs the base graph to be KNRS, and the KNRS conjecture is widely open. Theorem 1.4 removes that need only under the divisibility condition, and the authors cannot treat subdivisions with different path lengths. For the 1-subdivision of an arbitrary graph H (one path of length 2 per edge), the sum in Theorem 1.4 is e(H), which meets the condition only when e(H) = binom(h,2), that is, when H is complete; so the 1-subdivision of an arbitrary graph is not settled here.

relevance.text: No result of this paper decides the girth-six statement. Its results give special cases of the statement, that is, Sidorenko graphs of girth at least six: the 1-subdivision of a KNRS graph (the Conlon, Kim, Lee and Lee result restated here; every 1-subdivision of a simple graph has girth at least six), uniform subdivisions of Sidorenko graphs, whose girth is at least 8 (Proposition 4.2), and even-path replacements under the divisibility condition, for example every edge of a graph H on h vertices replaced by m internally disjoint paths of length 4 with m e(H) >= binom(h,2), whose girth is at least 8 (Theorem 1.4). Conjecture 4.1 is a declared neighbour. A subdivision of a Sidorenko graph has a 4-cycle exactly when some 4-cycle of the base graph keeps all four edges unsubdivided, and a cubic girth-six graph such as the Heawood graph is a subdivision only of itself, so neither statement implies the other. Lemma 2.2 is the regular-graphon reduction: in a d-regular graphon a vertex of degree one contributes exactly a factor d to the density.
